sources.search_query: Japan foreign ministry official visa exemption list tourist mofa.go.jp
sources.relevant_excerpt: Passport holders from specific countries and regions can enter Japan visa-free for 90 days or less if engaging solely in tourism activities (complete list at the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs website: mofa.go.jp/j_info/visit/visa/short/novisa.html). "Most short-term stays allow up to 90 days. Some nationalities may be granted 15, 30, or 180 days." For visa applicants: "Depending on your circumstances you may require: - Visa application form - Valid passport - Recent photo - Accommodation Reservation Confirmation or Itinerary - Proof of sufficient funds to cover your trip"; processing typically takes around five business days. JNTO (Japan National Tourism Organization) is the Government of Japan's official tourism organization; the page links MOFA visa requirements (mofa.go.jp/j_info/visit/visa/index.html) and the MOFA embassy directory (mofa.go.jp/about/emb_cons/mofaserv.html).

conditions: Visa-free entry applies to short-term stays for tourism and similar Temporary Visitor activities only (no paid work).

Period of stay is granted in units of up to 90, 30 or 15 days depending on the nationality's arrangement; the per-nationality period could not be verified because MOFA's canonical exemption page was unreachable (HTTP 403). JNTO states most nationalities receive up to 90 days.
GBR: applies to British citizens only (per ISA specified-country list conditions).
IDN and ARE: ISA notes these passports are subject to visa-exemption registration or travel-authorization conditions at Japanese overseas missions; exact conditions unverified (MOFA unreachable).
TWN: Taiwan passport holders; HKG: Hong Kong SAR passport holders; MAC: Macao SAR passport holders.

List taken from the ISA specified-country list, defined as countries/regions for which Japan maintains visa-exemption measures excluding those whose exemption is suspended or subject to visa-obtainment-recommendation measures. One or more entries (e.g. Hungary, which appears on MOFA's published list) may be missing from this extraction — see unresolved.
These nationalities are covered by Japan's visa-exemption measures for short-term tourism, so no tourist visa is required for an exempt short-term stay.

dispositions.maximum_stay: granted in units of up to 90, 30 or 15 days (Temporary Visitor status)
conditions: Not included in Japan's visa-exemption specified-country list; per ISA, foreign nationals other than those of visa-exempt countries/regions require a visa in addition to a valid passport.

Visas are applied for through Japanese embassies/consulates (JNTO describes the application documents and ~5 business days processing); office-level procedures, accredited-agency requirements (e.g. for Chinese nationals) and any mandated visa centers could not be verified because MOFA and emb-japan.go.jp sites returned HTTP 403.

An online JAPAN eVISA channel may exist for some of these nationalities/countries of residence, but it could not be verified from any reachable official source (evisa.mofa.go.jp returned HTTP 403) — see unresolved.

dispositions.maximum_stay: granted in units of up to 90, 30 or 15 days (Temporary Visitor status)
conditions: Per ISA, a valid passport and a visa are required for entry except for nationals of visa-exempt countries/regions.
Application is made before travel through Japanese overseas missions; details unverified because MOFA/embassy sites returned HTTP 403.
An online JAPAN eVISA channel may exist for some nationalities/countries of residence but could not be verified from a reachable official source.
Japan is the destination; Japanese citizens are not subject to the visa regime for foreign nationals (ISA entry requirements apply to foreign nationals, 外国人).

Japan does not currently operate an electronic travel authorization for tourism. JESTA (電子渡航認証制度) was created by the Reiwa-8 (2026) immigration law amendment but its provisions take effect on a date to be set by cabinet order no later than 2029-03-31; it is not in operation as of 2026-07-23.

Official ISA guidance describes only two channels for short-term entry: visa-exempt entry for listed countries/regions, or a visa obtained before travel; no tourist visa-on-arrival program is described on any reachable official page.

policies.policy_name: Japan short-term stay visa exemption arrangements (査証免除措置)
policies.description: Japan maintains visa-exemption measures for nationals of listed countries/regions for short-term stays (Temporary Visitor status: tourism, recreation, visiting relatives, sightseeing, meetings, business liaison and similar activities; no paid work). The ISA 'specified country' list enumerates the countries/regions for which Japan currently maintains visa-exemption measures, excluding countries whose exemption is temporarily suspended or subject to visa-obtainment-recommendation measures. Period of stay is granted in units of up to 90, 30 or 15 days; JNTO states most nationalities receive up to 90 days.
conditions: Tourism and other Temporary Visitor activities only; no paid work, long-term study or residency.
GBR entry limited to British citizens.
IDN and ARE subject to registration/travel-authorization conditions per the ISA list; details unverified.
Canonical per-country stay periods are published by MOFA (novisa.html), which was unreachable (HTTP 403); list here may be missing entries (e.g. Hungary).
policies.maximum_stay: up to 90 days (units of 90, 30 or 15 days depending on nationality)

policies.policy_name: Short-term stay (Temporary Visitor) visa via Japanese overseas missions
policies.description: Foreign nationals not covered by a visa-exemption arrangement must hold a valid passport and obtain a visa before travel. Per ISA: nationals of visa-exempt countries/regions need no visa; all others require one. JNTO describes the application (form, valid passport, photo, accommodation/itinerary, proof of funds) with processing typically around five business days, and refers applicants to Japanese embassies/consulates via the MOFA directory.
conditions: Details of consular procedures, fees, accredited travel-agency requirements (e.g. for Chinese nationals) and any mandated visa application centers could not be verified: MOFA and emb-japan.go.jp sites returned HTTP 403.
policies.maximum_stay: granted in units of up to 90, 30 or 15 days (Temporary Visitor status)

policies.policy_name: JESTA (Japan Electronic System for Travel Authorization) — enacted, not yet in force
policies.description: The Reiwa-8 (2026) amendment to the Immigration Control Act creates JESTA, an electronic travel authorization system. The creating provisions take effect on a date to be fixed by cabinet order no later than 31 March 2029 (令和11年3月31日). JESTA is NOT operational as of 2026-07-23; no traveler currently needs or can obtain a Japanese ETA.
conditions: Not yet in force; scope of covered nationalities (expected to target visa-exempt travelers) not specified on the fetched page.

passport_validity.condition_text: ISA requires 我が国が承認した外国政府等の発行した有効な旅券 (a valid passport issued by a foreign government recognized by Japan) for entry. No minimum validity period beyond the stay and no blank-page rule was found on any reachable official page; MOFA pages that might state more were unreachable (HTTP 403).

unresolved: MOFA (www.mofa.go.jp) returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt: /j_info/visit/visa/short/novisa.html, /j_info/visit/visa/, /j_info/visit/Visa/short/novisa.html, /j_info/visit/visa/short/novisa.html?p=1, /j_info/visit/visa/basics.html. The canonical visa-exemption list with per-country stay periods (90/30/15 days), visa fee schedule, and eVisa program pages could therefore not be verified directly.

JAPAN eVISA portal (https://www.evisa.mofa.go.jp/index) returned HTTP 403. The eVisa program's existence, eligible nationalities/countries of residence, stay length and fees could not be verified from any reachable official source, so NO evisa_tourist disposition rows were recorded. Some non-exempt nationalities may in fact have an online eVISA application channel; treat the EMBASSY_VISA_REQUIRED rows as the default channel only.

Embassy of Japan sites all returned HTTP 403 (us.emb-japan.go.jp/itpr_en/visa.html, uk.emb-japan.go.jp/itpr_en/visa.html, sg.emb-japan.go.jp/itpr_en/visa_top.html), so consular procedures, authorized visa application centers (e.g. JVAC/VFS in some jurisdictions) and accredited-agency requirements for specific nationalities (e.g. CHN) are unverified; no authorized_visa_center portal recorded.
Government visa fees (typically quoted by MOFA in local currency equivalent of JPY amounts for single/double/multiple-entry visas) are unverified — fees array left empty rather than guessed.
Per-nationality maximum stay under the exemption (e.g. shorter periods for THA, IDN, BRN, QAT, ARE) unverified; JNTO states most nationalities receive up to 90 days and some 15/30/180 days.

The exemption list was extracted from the ISA specified-country page (a TTP pre-check reference defined as countries with active visa-exemption measures). Hungary, which appears on MOFA's published exemption list per search-result snippets (not evidence), was absent from the extraction — possible extraction gap; the list may be missing one or more entries.

http://www.moj.go.jp/ENGLISH/information/bpic3rd-03.html (English statement of the passport+visa landing principle) returned 404; https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/en/ returned 404; https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/applications/guide/kanri_qa.html returned an effectively empty page. English-language ISA confirmation of the entry principle is therefore missing; the principle is sourced from the Japanese ISA Q&A page.

Visit Japan Web (services.digital.go.jp/en/visit-japan-web/, linked from JNTO) is an arrival-procedures service, not a visa/ETA, and per JNTO is not mandatory; not recorded as a portal since no matching portal_kind applies.
